title: The Stubai Höhenweg Hut Circuit

bestPeriod.note: The Peiljoch and Niederl saddles hold hard snow into early July; late September brings the first hut closures.

summary: A six-hut circuit around the Stubai Alps from Neustift, crossing five glacier-rimmed saddles between 2,700 m and 3,000 m.
hook: The Stubai Höhenweg is a ring of Alpenverein huts strung around a horseshoe of 3,000 m peaks, and you spend the week walking the inside of that horseshoe with the glaciers never far from view. Every day ends at a staffed hut with a hot meal and a bed, and every day in between crosses a saddle that makes you work for the next valley. Neustift, at the mouth of the Stubaital, is the only base you need.

snapshot.Base(s): Neustift im Stubaital (start/finish), six huts en route
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 60–68 km, 5,600 m ascent / 5,600 m descent; high alpine path on scree, slab and moraine, T3 with T4 sections
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Innsbruck (INN), then IVB regional bus 4166 up the Stubaital to Neustift (about 40 minutes)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Fit hikers with hut experience and no fear of exposed, cable-secured ground; not a first alpine trek

itinerary.title: Neustift to Starkenburger Hütte
itinerary.morning: Bus or taxi from Neustift to the Kampl trailhead above Fulpmes, or walk straight out of Neustift village if you want the full vertical. Either way the path climbs through spruce forest onto the open Schlick valley flank.
itinerary.afternoon: Steady switchbacks above the treeline to Starkenburger Hütte (2,237 m), an Alpenverein hut with a wide terrace looking straight down the Stubaital. Book it in advance through the Alpenverein's online hut-booking portal; July and August weekends fill two to three weeks out.
itinerary.evening: Dinner is Tiroler Gröstl or a hut goulash; pay the overnight fee in cash, as most Stubai huts still prefer it for lodging even when the bar takes cards.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 1,300 m ascent, negligible descent, 4.5–5.5 hours. Grade T2–T3, forest track then open alpine path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Starkenburger Hütte to Franz-Senn-Hütte
itinerary.morning: The path contours north below the Kalkwand and drops briefly into the Oberbergtal before climbing again — an undulating traverse rather than one clean pass, past the Bremer Hütte junction (worth the 20-minute detour for coffee if the timing works).
itinerary.afternoon: A final pull over rough moraine brings you to Franz-Senn-Hütte (2,147 m), one of the largest and oldest huts in the range, with its own small alpine museum and a view straight up the Alpeiner Ferner glacier.
itinerary.evening: The Franz-Senn-Hütte's kitchen runs late for a hut; a Kaiserschmarrn here is a fair reward. Book through the DAV/ÖAV portal — this hut sells out fastest of the six.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 850 m ascent, 650 m descent, 5–6 hours. Grade T3, exposed traverse sections with fixed cable on the steepest rock steps.

itinerary.title: Franz-Senn-Hütte to Dresdner Hütte
itinerary.morning: The big day. Climb past the Alpeiner Ferner's lower moraine to the Schwarzenbergscharte (2,919 m), a narrow notch with fixed steel cable on both approaches — the first genuinely alpine crossing of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend scree and old snow patches (common into mid-July) into the Gletschertal, then climb again to Dresdner Hütte (2,308 m), the circuit's biggest hut, sitting directly below the Stubai glacier ski area's lift infrastructure.
itinerary.evening: Dresdner Hütte has real showers and a bigger dining room than most; it is also the easiest hut to reach by cable car from Mutterberg, so it fills with day visitors as well as trekkers. Book ahead regardless.
itinerary.dayStats: 15 km, 950 m ascent, 800 m descent, 6–7 hours. Grade T4 at the Schwarzenbergscharte (fixed cable, exposed), T3 elsewhere. Snow risk: the scharte's north side can hold névé into early July — carry poles at minimum, microspikes are sensible before mid-July.

itinerary.title: Dresdner Hütte to Nürnberger Hütte
itinerary.morning: Climb past the glacier ski lifts (surreal in July, with skiers overhead on the Eisgrat) to the Peiljoch (2,997 m), the highest point on the whole circuit and a genuine mountaineer's saddle with cable protection on the final metres.
itinerary.afternoon: A long, knee-testing descent past the Sulzenauferner's outwash into the Neder valley, then a short reclimb to Nürnberger Hütte (2,297 m), tucked under the Wilder Freiger.
itinerary.evening: Quieter than Dresdner or Franz-Senn; a good hut for an early night before the next crossing.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, 750 m ascent, 950 m descent, 6 hours. Grade T4 at Peiljoch (short fixed-cable scramble, real exposure), T3 on the descent. Old snow on the Peiljoch's shaded side into July.

itinerary.title: Nürnberger Hütte to Sulzenauhütte
itinerary.morning: Drop into the valley floor near the Grünausee, a small glacial lake worth the five-minute detour, then begin the climb to the Niederl (2,700 m).
itinerary.afternoon: The Niederl is broad and less exposed than the previous two saddles, but the approach crosses a stretch of permanent scree that shifts underfoot — go slowly. Beyond it, Sulzenauhütte (2,191 m) sits below the Sulzenauferner glacier with the best glacier panorama of the week from its terrace.
itinerary.evening: This hut is popular with day-trippers from the Stubai valley floor via the Grawa waterfall path, so the terrace is lively; the dorms quiet down fast after 21:00.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 650 m ascent, 850 m descent, 5 hours. Grade T3, one loose scree traverse, no fixed protection required.

itinerary.title: Sulzenauhütte to Neue Regensburger Hütte
itinerary.morning: Climb to the Grawagrubennieder (2,900 m), the last of the big saddles, with views back over the whole horseshoe you have just walked.
itinerary.afternoon: The descent into the Oberissalm side is long and rocky; the Neue Regensburger Hütte (2,286 m) appears late, perched above the Oberiss reservoir.
itinerary.evening: This is the most remote of the six huts and the one most likely to have space without weeks of notice — still book ahead, but it is the fallback if others are full.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, 800 m ascent, 750 m descent, 6 hours. Grade T3–T4, short fixed-cable step below the saddle, exposure moderate.

itinerary.title: Neue Regensburger Hütte to Neustift
itinerary.morning: A long, mostly downhill walk past the Oberiss reservoir and into the Milders valley on a good path used by farm traffic in the lower half.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in Milders or Neustift by early-to-mid afternoon; the regional bus runs frequently back into Neustift centre if you finish in Milders.
itinerary.evening: A last Tiroler dinner in Neustift — Bacher Wirt or any of the Gasthöfe on the main street serve knödel and Kaspressknödelsuppe without pretension.
itinerary.dayStats: 15 km, 100 m ascent, 1,650 m descent, 4.5–5.5 hours. Grade T1–T2, farm track and forest road, no exposure.

accommodationStrategy.name: Alpenverein huts en route
accommodationStrategy.description: All six huts (Starkenburger, Franz-Senn, Dresdner, Nürnberger, Sulzenau, Neue Regensburger) are ÖAV/DAV huts bookable through the Alpenvereinshütten online reservation system; a handful still take direct phone bookings when the online calendar shows a hut as full but a warden holds back emergency beds. Book the full week as one block the day online reservations open for the season — Franz-Senn and Dresdner sell out first.
accommodationStrategy.booking: as early as the season's booking window allows, minimum 6–8 weeks ahead for August.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €25–€40 half-board per night for Alpenverein members, €45–€60 for non-members (join the Alpenverein or a reciprocal club before the trip — it pays for itself in three nights)

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Jagdhof or a Gasthof in Neustift
accommodationStrategy.description: Neustift has a deep bench of family-run hotels used to trekkers dropping bags before and after the circuit; ask any of them about secure luggage storage for the six days you are on the huts, which most offer informally.

accommodationStrategy.name: Self-catering apartment in Neustift or Fulpmes
accommodationStrategy.description: A cheaper way to cover the arrival and departure nights, with a kitchen for restocking hut snacks before you start.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Austrian alpine rescue (Bergrettung) is reached fastest on **140**. Every hut has a landline and usually a radio even where mobile signal fails.
logistics.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms build from around 13:00 in July and August; start each stage by 07:00–07:30 to be off the saddles before the build-up.
logistics.bookingWindows: The Alpenvereinshütten portal opens hut calendars roughly 6–12 months ahead depending on the hut; Franz-Senn and Dresdner (glacier-adjacent, cable-car accessible) fill first because they also serve day visitors and via-ferrata parties.

other.label: Hüttenschlafsack is mandatory
other.text: , not optional — huts will rent one if you forget, but at a markup, and it is one more thing to queue for at check-in.

other.label: Cash for huts
other.text: Bar tabs and lodging at most huts still run on cash; carry €300–€400 in €20s and €50s for the week, since the nearest ATM after Neustift is nonexistent until you return.

other.label: Snow on the saddles
other.text: Schwarzenbergscharte, Peiljoch and Grawagrubennieder can all hold hard old snow into the first half of July; ask the hut warden the evening before, since they update conditions daily.

other.label: Camping is prohibited
other.text: in the Tyrolean alpine zone outside designated sites — the huts are the accommodation, not a fallback for a tent.

proTips: Reserve the whole six-hut chain the same day the booking calendar opens; a broken chain is the single most common thing that unravels this trip.
Carry a printed confirmation for each hut — a warden checking a paper list moves faster than one hunting for a booking app with patchy signal.
Eat the Kaiserschmarrn at Franz-Senn-Hütte before 15:00, before the afternoon rush from the Alpeiner Ferner trail arrives.
Fill water bottles at every hut tap without exception — above 2,200 m there is almost no reliable surface water between saddles.
Cross the Peiljoch and Schwarzenbergscharte before 10:00; loose scree that is frozen firm at dawn turns to ball-bearings by early afternoon.
Ask each warden about the next day's saddle conditions at dinner — huts compare notes by radio and know about fresh snow before any app does.
If a saddle is genuinely bad, the valley-floor alternative from most huts is a straightforward descent to a Stubaital bus stop.

packingNotes: Hüttenschlafsack (hut sleeping liner) — genuinely mandatory, not a suggestion, at every ÖAV/DAV hut.
A headtorch with spare batteries for dorm rooms and pre-dawn starts.
Trekking poles, non-negotiable for the long descents on Days 3, 4 and 7.
Microspikes or light crampons if walking before mid-July, for old snow on the three high saddles.
A 30–40 L pack that carries well loaded — you are on your feet 5–7 hours most days.
Cash in small notes, more than feels necessary.
A lightweight hard-shell — the exposed saddles get genuine wind even on a clear day.
What people over-pack: a full change of clothes for each day. Two hiking sets and one dry hut set is enough.
What people under-pack: sun protection. The glacier-adjacent saddles reflect UV hard even in cloud.
whatCouldGoWrong: **A hut in the chain is full.** Fallback: Neue Regensburger and Sulzenauhütte usually have more late availability than Franz-Senn or Dresdner; a broken chain can sometimes be patched by descending to the valley for one night and rejoining by bus and a shorter re-ascent the next day.
**Old snow on a saddle you're not equipped for.** Fallback: ask the warden the evening before; most huts can suggest a lower, longer alternative path that avoids the steepest snow-holding gully.

**Afternoon storm building on a saddle.** Fallback: turn back to the hut you left rather than push over an exposed crossing — every saddle on this circuit has a hut within 1–2 hours behind you for most of the ascent.
**Knees give out on the long descents.** Days 3, 4 and 7 drop 750–1,650 m each. Fallback: poles from day one, and a rest morning built around a late start rather than skipping a hut night.

**Bus timing back from Milders or Neustift.** Fallback: the Stubaital regional bus runs regularly in season, but confirm the last departure the night before at the hut, since Day 7 timing depends on how the descent goes.
